title: Ramayana Advance Booking Crosses 2 Lakh Tickets in National Chains for Opening Day
excerpt: PVR Inox and Cinepolis sales for the November 5 opener rose from 1.70 lakh on Saturday to about 2 lakh by Sunday night, with all-India advances at 4.58 lakh tickets.
body:
• Ramayana: Part One has sold about 2 lakh tickets for its opening day in India's top two national chains, PVR Inox and Cinepolis, as of 11:45 p.m. on November 1, Pinkvilla reported.
  • That is up from 1.70 lakh tickets in the same chains on Saturday afternoon — the 2 lakh mark Bollywood Hungama had projected the film would cross by the end of Sunday.
  • Across all of India, Sacnilk data put opening-day advance sales at 4.58 lakh tickets and Rs 20.32 crore excluding blocked seats, across 13,317 shows.
  • The Hindi-language epic, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and starring Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi, opens on Thursday, November 5, in the Diwali festive window.

Advance booking for Ramayana: Part One crossed a round number on Sunday night. As of 11:45 p.m. on November 1, the film had sold about 2 lakh tickets for its opening day in India's top two national chains, PVR Inox and Cinepolis, according to Pinkvilla. The film opens on Thursday, November 5.

The climb

The national-chains figure has moved quickly. Bollywood Hungama reported 1.70 lakh tickets sold in the same chains as of 3 p.m. on Saturday, October 31, and projected the film would hit 2 lakh by the end of Sunday — which is what Pinkvilla's Sunday-night count shows. Pinkvilla reported that IMAX screens are filling fast, with almost all prime seats booked. The two trade reports differ on how far bookings have spread beyond the big chains: Hungama said advances had begun opening in non-national chains, while Pinkvilla said full-fledged advances in non-national chains, single screens and South Indian markets were still to open.

The bigger all-India picture

The national chains are only part of the advance. Sacnilk data reported on November 1 put opening-day advance sales across India at 4.58 lakh tickets and Rs 20.32 crore excluding blocked seats (Rs 24.15 crore and 5.51 lakh tickets including them), across 13,317 shows. For the first two days combined, the advance stood at Rs 30.24 crore excluding blocked seats. These figures are distinct from the circuit-wide number quoted by PVR Inox's Executive Director Sanjeev Kumar Bijli on October 30 — advance bookings crossing 2.5 lakh tickets across the PVR Inox circuit for the festive window as a whole, not opening day alone.

"The response to Ramayana has been very encouraging, with advance bookings crossing 2.5 lakh tickets across the PVR INOX circuit. The film's opening during a six day festive window is well timed, as this is traditionally a period when families come together and cinema becomes a natural part of the celebrations."

— Sanjeev Kumar Bijli, Executive Director, PVR INOX

The film and the diaspora

Ramayana: Part One is a Hindi-language epic directed by Nitesh Tiwari, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi and Ravie Dubey. Its November 5 release lands in the Diwali festive window. The India advance is a separate story from the overseas presales The Videshi reported on October 30 — 88,772 tickets worth $1.7 million in the US and Canada — and diaspora audiences in North America, Australia and the UK have been booking since presales opened there on October 15. Trade trackers expect the advance to surge through the final stretch from Monday to the day before release; Pinkvilla cautions that its figures are trade estimates, not final collections.
